content:
Talia Benson: hey infra folks — kicking off the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint. we need to reserve H100 capacity for ~2 weeks (mostly daytime PT). goal is to run the full matrix + reruns without stepping on Dedicated pools. can we lock windows + get a cost sanity check?

Talia Benson: rough ask (can refine):
- H100 SXM (80GB) preferred
- 256–384 GPU-hours/day for days 3–8 (matrix runs), then smaller for analysis/reruns
- regions: us-east + us-west; would love 1 EU cluster if it’s cheap-ish
- hard requirement: no Dedicated pool impact

Irene Choi: yep, tracking. couple qs:
1) are you ok with spot-like preemptions or must be hard reserved?
2) single-node runs (8xH100) or spread across nodes?
3) do you need consistent driver/CUDA across clusters (we can pin images but it limits where we can place)

Talia Benson: must be hard reserved for the matrix window (we got burned by preemptions last sprint). mix is fine (8x nodes + smaller) but ideally 8xH100 nodes for runner simplicity. yes on pinned driver/CUDA.

Vanessa Ortiz: we can do hard reservations but need exact windows so we can fence off from customer pools. also: please confirm you’ll run in the bench namespace / bench queue only.

Talia Benson: yes, bench namespace only. can share job labels we’ll set.

Rina Kobayashi: we’ll tag jobs with:
- `team=serving-runtime`
- `purpose=benchmark`
- `project=fp8-int8-sprint`
- `no-preempt=true`
we can also set `cluster_role=bench` if that helps scheduler routing.

Irene Choi: helpful. we have 3 relevant H100 pools right now:
- `gpu-prod-us-east1-h100-sxm` (mostly Dedicated pressure)
- `gpu-prod-us-west2-h100-sxm` (some slack overnight PT)
- `gpu-bench-us-central1-h100-pcie` (bench-only, but PCIe not SXM)
EU H100 is tight (and $$$). we can likely give you:
- us-west2: 6 nodes (48 GPUs) 18:00–10:00 PT daily
- us-central bench: 4 nodes (32 GPUs) 08:00–18:00 PT daily
that gets you ~80 H100s/day w/ clean isolation, but mixed SXM/PCIe.

Hiro Tanaka: mixed SXM/PCIe is ok if we separate reporting by SKU (we already do). biggest need is “noisy neighbor” free + stable clocks.

Vanessa Ortiz: re: Dedicated pool conflicts — we can’t touch `gpu-prod-us-east1-h100-sxm` during biz hours (too many reserved contracts). if you need east, it’d have to be a small slice + only in the bench partition.

Talia Benson: prefer to avoid prod-east entirely if it’s going to be risky. can we do west + central only and call that sufficient?

Rafael Mendes: +1 from SRE side: please don’t run big bench jobs in prod-east. last time we had a Dedicated throughput blip and spent a day unwinding it.

Irene Choi: ok. on clocking: we can lock application clocks in bench clusters, but we need you to run on the “bench” node class (has admin hooks enabled). you’ll get a short doc w/ commands.

Keiko Yamamoto: also adding a guardrail: autoscaler will treat bench reservations as “fixed”; if you exceed reservation, overflow won’t schedule onto prod H100 pools. so please keep your runner’s max concurrency <= reserved GPUs.

Rina Kobayashi: our matrix runner can cap concurrency per pool. we’ll set:
- west2 max=48
- central bench max=32
and keep a 10–15% buffer for reruns.

Vanessa Ortiz: cool. scheduling windows proposal (PT):
- west2 H100 SXM: 18:00–10:00 daily (48 GPUs)
- central bench H100 PCIe: 08:00–18:00 daily (32 GPUs)
that covers “daytime” via central and “overnight” via west. any reason you need a single contiguous 12h+ window on one pool?

Talia Benson: no, split is fine. we’ll treat them as separate lanes.

Irene Choi: cost estimate (ballpark, internal rates):
- H100 SXM: ~$4.75/GPU-hr
- H100 PCIe: ~$3.60/GPU-hr
If you run ~48*16 + 32*10 = 1,088 GPU-hr/day at max (you probably won’t), that’s ~$4.6k/day. For 10 heavy days, call it $40–50k range incl reruns + headroom.

Talia Benson: got it. we can justify that.

Neha Kapoor: jumping in — $50k range is fine for this sprint as long as we (a) don’t impact Dedicated and (b) capture artifacts + results in a reusable way. consider this approval to proceed. :thumbsup:

Vanessa Ortiz: :thumbsup: noted. we’ll still need a paper trail for finance — please open/attach the internal quota ticket (INT-9923?) and link this thread.

Talia Benson: will do today.

FleetBot: Reservation request draft created: `bench-resv/fp8-int8-sprint` (status: PENDING). Requested resources: 48x H100-SXM (us-west2), 32x H100-PCIe (us-central1). Windows: west2 18:00–10:00 PT; central1 08:00–18:00 PT. Owner: @Vanessa Ortiz.

Irene Choi: also: we need pinned stack for benchmarking. recommend:
- driver 550.54.15
- cuda 12.4 base
- container image: `runtime-bench:1.22.0-rc3`
if you need a different combo, say now bc cross-cluster mismatch has bitten us.

Hiro Tanaka: we’re on 12.4 + that driver in the harness PR. `runtime-bench:1.22.0-rc3` works.

Rina Kobayashi: +1. also we’ll disable MIG and set persistence mode on. will follow your doc for app clocks.

Keiko Yamamoto: for avoidance of Dedicated pool collisions, please include these node selectors in the runner by default:
```
node_selector:
  redwood.io/pool: bench
  redwood.io/gpu_sku: h100
  redwood.io/is_dedicated: "false"
```
and label jobs with `bench_reservation=fp8-int8-sprint` so we can audit.

Rina Kobayashi: ack. we’ll bake that into the runner config.

Vanessa Ortiz: timeline check: when do you need the reservations active?

Talia Benson: ideally starting tomorrow 08:00 PT for calibration runs, then heavy matrix starting day after.

Irene Choi: we can turn on central bench window tomorrow AM. west2 window starts tonight 18:00 PT. you’ll get access to the reservation IDs + kube contexts in a separate DM.

Rafael Mendes: pls also drop the reservation IDs in #eng-runtime once you have them so folks know where to run (and where NOT to run).

Talia Benson: will do. thanks all.

Neha Kapoor: final note: if you see any contention signals (queue depth spikes, unexpected throttling), stop the run and ping infra immediately. don’t “power through” on prod pools.

Talia Benson: 100%. we’ll keep it in bench lanes only.

FleetBot: Reservation `bench-resv/fp8-int8-sprint` status updated: APPROVED. Enforcement: overflow scheduling to prod pools DISABLED. Contact: @Vanessa Ortiz / @Irene Choi.
